hook: SCP-3780 takes the 1963 assassination of John F. Kennedy in Dallas and treats it as a containment problem. The twist is in the premise: the Foundation's job here is to make sure the shooting happens on schedule. Read it as a dry comedy of logistics; the list of attempts is where it shines.
whyItMatters: It inverts the familiar time-travel plot, where someone goes back to stop a tragedy, by casting the Foundation as the side defending the original timeline. The justification is pure Foundation thinking: stopping the assassination would change nothing significant, yet a single objective timeline must be preserved anyway. Names that carry their own tags, such as Marshall, Carter and Dark and Dr. Thaddeus Xyank, also turn up along the way.
thingsToNotice:
Each entry pairs a rescue attempt with the countermeasure that undoes it, and the escalation is the joke. A rival gunman in the depository is gut-shot from the grassy knoll; an Oswald who vanishes at 12:29 and reappears at 12:42 is quietly sent back to the moment he vanished; an MC&D agent trying to abort him before birth with powdered unicorn horn in his mother's milk is caught after an overnight stakeout. All of it is logged as calmly as routine maintenance.

The standout is Dr. Xyank brawling with his own future self, each one arriving five seconds after the other to knock him out and shove him through a gateway, until Kennedy is already dead and both agree to a truce. The final attempt turns darker, with a Tau-5 team sent by a future Foundation to kill Oswald, a present-day Tau-5 dispatched to stop its own future selves, and diplomatic channels opened with that later Foundation to learn why. The closing pointer to 'Extended Incident Logs' refers to material not on this page, so the list here is only a selection.
